## Detailed Findings

#### 1. Cline #13476: Stored capability list tool-calling fix (LOW/SKIP)

- **What**: Multi-part fix for custom OpenAI-compatible models where synthesized/stored/migrated capability lists silently revoked tool calling. toStoredModelInfo synthesized capabilities from boolean flags (supportsReasoning: true -> ["reasoning"]) but omitted "tools", runtime gate read non-empty tool-less list as authoritative denial and dropped every tool. Three fixes: (1) seed "tools" when capability list synthesized from boolean flags, (2) treat stored/user-authored partial lists as non-authoritative for tool calling and seed "tools" into any non-empty list for language models (only generated catalog capabilities remain authoritative), (3) make legacy migration write "tools" into fabricated arrays to stop poisoning models.json.
- **Why**: Custom models with partial capability lists (e.g. `["prompt-cache"]` from UI or migration) lost tool calling entirely, breaking sessions.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/commit/13476 (Cline #13476)
- **Category**: provider
- **Size**: LOW (Alexi routing-config.json stores model `strengths/costTier/reasoning/maxTokens` metadata but NO preserved-capabilities field system like Cline's models.json, sapOrchestration.ts ORCHESTRATION_MODEL_METADATA is hardcoded not user-editable, pattern only relevant if Alexi adds user-editable model capability persistence where partial lists can be stored, ~6h to add empty-array guard + synthesis seeding + authoritative vs non-authoritative capability distinction IF capability persistence lands). SKIP for now — Alexi's model metadata is read-only config files, no user-editable capability storage, no capability synthesis from boolean flags.

#### 2. Cline #13468: Hub drain/upgrade with durable event log + run queue (MODERATE-HIGH infrastructure / SKIP - TOO LARGE)

- **What**: Production-grade hub infrastructure: SQLite-backed durable event log + run queue + instance locking + drain/upgrade commands + bot profiles + replay-after-sequence for graceful daemon upgrades. HubEventLogStore persists all events (sequence/eventId/envelope) with append + replayEventsAfter, HubRunQueue tracks pending work (runId/status/payload), HubInstanceLock ensures singleton daemon via SQLite advisory lock, `cline hub drain` stops accepting new work + waits for idle + triggers upgrade, `cline hub upgrade --wait N` checks idleness + spawns new daemon + replays events from old daemon's last sequence so no events lost during upgrade. WebSocket transport tracks sinceSequence cursor + dedupes by eventId, bot profiles define identity/rules/plugins for hub-backed agents.
- **Why**: Graceful daemon upgrades without dropping in-flight work, multi-client hub orchestration with durable event sourcing, production-grade reliability for long-running agents.
- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/13468 (Cline #13468)
- **Category**: config | server (hub infrastructure spans multiple categories)
- **Size**: MODERATE-HIGH infrastructure (~24h+ to implement full hub with SQLite-backed event log + durable run queue + instance locking + drain/upgrade commands + WebSocket transport + bot profiles + replay support). Alexi src/core/database/database.ts has basic SQLite helpers (PRAGMA, busy timeout) + src/server/socket.ts has UNIX socket daemon for remote slash commands but NO hub features: NO durable event logs, NO run queues beyond in-memory session state, NO drain/upgrade lifecycle, NO multi-client WebSocket hub, NO bot profiles, NO instance locking, NO event replay. Pattern valuable for production-grade daemon orchestration + graceful upgrades + multi-agent coordination but LARGE scope — defer until hub architecture decision made, too large for auto-implement (needs design phase: hub vs current socket server, multi-client vs single-session, event sourcing strategy, SQLite vs alternatives, bot profiles vs existing agent system). SKIP for immediate action — track as strategic feature for future hub roadmap.
